samples.summary: Crop/text-edit teardown tests can't distinguish 'discard' from 'commit'
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` deliberately calls `exitImageCrop(false)` and `exitEditMode('cancel')` (editor.ts:1550-1551), and both the source comment and the test comment ("so it is discarded rather than committed — a commit would write to nowhere", test:267-268) present that as the behavior under test. But the assertions are only `expect(ed.isCropping()).toBe(false)` (test:272) and `expect(ed.isTextEditing()).toBe(false)` (test:248) — both hold identically if the code were changed to `exitImageCrop(true)` / `exitEditMode('commit')`, since commit also exits the session. Nothing asserts the store was not mutated (e.g. comparing the element's crop rect / blocks in `store.read()` before and after, or that no extra undo entry was pushed), so the discard-vs-commit choice ships untested.
searchedFor: read whole current-slide-heal.test.ts looking for store.read()/undo assertions after heal

samples.summary: Empty-deck branch of resolveCurrentSlide has no test
samples.evidence: `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` intentionally leaves `currentId` dangling and skips the whole teardown (no listener notification, no selection clear, no crop/edit exit). The new suite never removes every slide — every test keeps at least one slide (`setup(2)`/`setup(3)` then removes one). So the behavior when the last slide is deleted while cropping/text-editing (session left alive against a nonexistent slide) is uncovered.
searchedFor: read current-slide-heal.test.ts fully (no removeSlides of all ids)

samples.summary: Upper clamp (Math.min against slides.length - 1) is never exercised
samples.evidence: Every heal test removes exactly one slide, so `currentIndex - 1` is always <= `doc.slides.length - 1` and the `Math.min` upper clamp is dead in the suite. No test removes several trailing slides at once (e.g. `removeSlides([id2, id3])` from a 4-slide deck with the cursor on the last one), which is the only case where the upper clamp matters.
searchedFor: looked for removeSlides calls with more than one id

samples.summary: Notification test asserts >0, so a double heal/notify would pass
samples.evidence: `expect(notified).toBeGreaterThan(0)` cannot catch the very failure mode the source comment at editor.ts:1539-1543 says it guards against (a nested resolve healing a second time and firing listeners again). Asserting the exact count (`toBe(1)`) is what would make the 'settles after one heal' claim testable; the separate 'settles after one heal' case only re-checks the final id, which is also stable under duplicate notifications.

samples.summary: No test asserts the canvas actually paints again after healing (the reported symptom)
samples.evidence: Issue #883's symptom quoted in the test header is "the canvas painted nothing". Every assertion in the suite reads only `getCurrentSlideId()` / `getSelection()` / `isCropping()` / `isTextEditing()`. Nothing observes the renderer (e.g. a spy/stub around SlideRenderer.render or a canvas pixel check) so a heal that fixed the id but still failed to repaint would pass the whole suite.

samples.summary: Heal via the repaintOverlay resolve site is untested
samples.evidence: There are two resolve sites (repaintOverlay editor.ts:1069 and render editor.ts:1427). The test helper `frame()` always does `markDirty(); render()`, so the render site always heals first and any later overlay resolve is a plain hit. A path where `repaintOverlay()` is the first resolver after the removal (which is what happens when a selection/overlay repaint runs before the next render frame) is never exercised — notably the teardown reentrancy the comment describes is only checked through the render entry point.
searchedFor: grep resolveCurrentSlide call sites in editor.ts

samples.summary: setCellSelection(null) on heal has no covering test
samples.evidence: The heal clears table cell-range selection, but no test sets a cell selection (no table element is created anywhere in the new suite) before removing the slide, so this line could be deleted without any test failing.

verdict.reason: Finding is half-refutable, not fully refutable. Crop half: the reviewer's claim that the test would stay green under `exitImageCrop(true)` is FALSE — commitCropFrame writes to the removed slide (editor.ts:2495-2512), MemSlidesStore.requireSlide throws 'Slide not found' (memory.ts:691-695, 1828-1831), exitImageCrop only has try/finally with no catch (editor.ts:2448-2461), render() does not guard resolveCurrentSlide (editor.ts:1426-1431), and the editor does not subscribe to store.onChange (editor.ts:269) so the throw is not eaten by notifyChange's listener catch (memory.ts:1783-1787); it escapes frame(ed) at test:270 and fails the test. Text half stands: exitEditMode('commit') routes through onCommit whose store write is wrapped in try/catch (editor.ts:4122-4163), so the write failure is swallowed and finishEditMode runs either way — isTextEditing()===false (test:248) holds under both 'commit' and 'cancel'. The only observable difference is a stray undo snapshot pushed by batch() before the throw (memory.ts:1789-1793), and no test asserts undo-stack state; a repo-wide search of packages/slides/test for heal/removeSlides and canUndo/undoStack turned up no other coverage of the heal teardown. One counterexample for one of the two named tests is not enough to drop the whole finding, so I leave it on the gate rather than refuting.
